The vehicle is equipped with a computer system that can indicate when to change the engine oil, oil filter, transmission oil, brake fluid and coolant. The change time depends on several factors, including engine speed, engine temperature, engine torque and mileage. Depending on driving conditions, the mileage when fluid change is indicated may vary greatly. To ensure proper operation of the vehicle intelligent maintenance system, the system must be reset every time the fluid is changed. Please refer to the Manual for details

Note:\nFront Crossing Traffic Braking is a safety assistance, which cannot completely replace the operation of the driver. The driver need to pay attention to road conditions at all times and drive safely.
Note:\nThe driver shall concentrate and shall not rely too much on this function, so as to avoid accidents. Please refer to the Manual for details

Front Cross Traffic Alert (FCTA) is a driving assistance feature that alerts the driver to potential collisions with vehicles or pedestrians crossing from the front while the driver is starting to move or at low speed in D mode. This system helps to enhance safety by warning the driver to take evasive action and avoid a potential accident

It refers to the function of activating/releasing Autohold by automatically identifying parking and driving. It can avoid frequent switching between gear-shifting and parking brake operation and simplify driving in case of following in traffic jams and holding at traffic lights
Note:\nBSD is ADAS system and cannot completely replace the driver\'s operation. The driver must focus on the road environment information and drive safely

When the system detects a target in the blind spot of the adjacent lane or a rapidly approaching target in the adjacent lane, the alarm indicator on the rearview mirror light on the corresponding side will turn on or flash to alert the driver. Please refer to the Manual for details

Blind Spot Information System includes Information Alert function and Collision Warning function. \nThe system monitors the side blind zone in real time and activates the Information Alert function when a cyclist appears in side blind zone, and activates the Collision Warning function when the risk of collision increases.

Note:\nThe information alert function is on by default and cannot be switched off by the driver; The collision warning function is on by default and can be switched off by the driver; BSIS is a safety assistance and only provides alert and warning. The driver needs to concentrate to maintain control of the vehicle and is responsible for driving safety. Please refer to the manual for details
Please turn off Navigate on Driving Assistant (NOA), and try again

Note:\nNavigate on Driving Assistant (NOA) is available for some highways covered by the ADAS Map and requires good road conditions such as clear lane lines and non-construction roads. Please refer to the Manual for details. When enabled, the driver is still responsible for the safety of the vehicle all the time. The driver must keep focused and take over the steering wheel when necessary
It is only valid for the current power-on cycle
This function is disabled when the vehicle stops and is shifted in gear P
Once turned on, turn it off by shifting gears or stepping on the accelerator pedal

Electronic Stability Control (ESC) OFF:\nIt analyses the vehicle driving state information transmitted from each sensor, and then sends deviation correction instructions to ABS and EBD to help the vehicle maintain dynamic balance. ESC can maintain the best stability of the vehicle under various conditions, and the effect is more obvious in the case of oversteer or understeer

Front Cross Traffic Brake (FCTB) is designed to avoid collision when driver drives out of parking spaces or accelerate through intersections and is about to collide with another vehicle crossing its path. The system will request the vehicle to slow down and send an alert to reduce the risk of collision. Please refer to the Manual for details

Note:\nIt is always the driver\'s responsibility to manually switch the high or low beam depending on traffic or weather conditions\nIHBC is an ADAS system, which cannot be guaranteed to be applicable to all driving situations. The driver must maintain full control of the vehicle and drive carefully

Intelligent High Beam Control (IHBC) can help the driver to use the high beam correctly. When the light switch is turned to the AUTO position and the light outside meets the conditions, the system will automatically switch between the low beam and the high beam in accordance with the current driving environment. Please refer to the Manual for details

Highway Navigate on Driving Assistant (HNOA) is a comfortable ADAS function, which applies to driving on some highways (covered by advanced ADAS maps) and allows lane change, obstacle avoidance, speed adjustment and other operations from point A to point B according to the navigation path under the effective monitoring by the driver

Note:\nHighway Navigate on Driving Assistant (HNOA) is available for some highways covered by the ADAS Map and requires good road conditions such as clear lane lines and non-construction roads. Please refer to the Manual for details. When enabled, the driver is still responsible for the safety of the vehicle all the time. The driver must keep focused and take over the steering wheel when necessary
Please turn off Intelligent Cruise Control (ICC), and try again

Interactive Lane Change Assist (ILCA) is a comfortable ADAS function based on Intelligent Cruise Control (ICC). It assists the driver in changing lane when the system receives commands from the driver\'s turn signal paddles

Note:\nILCA is an ADAS function. The driver must observe the driving environment when changing lane and hold the steering wheel all the time, to take over the steering wheel timely before the danger occurs
It does not allow overtaking on the inside lane when the driving speed is higher than 90 km/h (55 mph) \nTurn on Inside Overtaking Prevention (IOP)?
Note:\nThe driver shall concentrate and shall not rely too much on this function, so as to avoid accidents. Please refer to the user manual for details.

Inside Overtaking Prevention (IOP) is a driving assistance feature. When Adaptive Cruise Control (ACC)/Intelligent Cruise Control (ICC) is active and the vehicle is traveling at speeds above 90 km/h (55 mile/h), the system prevents the vehicle from overtaking on the inside of another vehicle
Note:\nLane Departure Assist is a safety assistance. Whether this function is activated or not, the driver needs to concentrate, maintain control of the vehicle, and be responsible for driving safety

Lane Departure Assist (LDA) includes Lane Departure Warning (LDW) and Lane Departure Prevention (LDP). LDW: When the vehicle speed exceeds a certain value, the system detects that the vehicle has unintentionally deviated from the lane; The instrument lane lines turn red, with sound or steering wheel vibration alerts; LDP: When the vehicle speed exceeds a certain value, the system provides steering assist to the driver to prevent the vehicle from deviating from its lane without the driver\'s awareness. When the lateral deviation speed of the vehicle is too high and the deviation prevention function cannot assist the vehicle back to its own lane in time, a deviation warning will be triggered. Please refer to the Manual for details

Intelligent Speed Limit Warning (ISLW) is an ADAS function. It monitors real-time road speed limit information and the driving speed, and alerts the driver in case of exceeding the speed limit to ensure safety
Note:\nISLC is ADAS system and cannot completely replace the driver\'s behaviour, and the driver must focus on the traffic sign information all the time

Intelligent Speed Limit Control (ISLC) is an integrated function of ACC and SLIF. If the cruising speed value is higher than the current road speed limit, the system can assist in controlling the driving speed within the road speed limit with the driver\'s confirmation. Please refer to the Manual for details

Moving Off Information System (MOIS) includes information alert function and collision warning function: It monitors and notifies the driver of the presence of a pedestrian in the front blind spot. MOIS activates the information alert function when the vehicle is starting or moving straight ahead at a speed of less than 10 km/h and when any pedestrian is present in the blind spot, and activates the collision warning function when the risk of collision increases

Note:\nThe information alert function and collision warning function are on by default and can be switched off by the driver; MOIS is a safety assistance and only provides alert and warning. The driver needs to concentrate to maintain control of the vehicle and is responsible for driving safety. Please refer to the manual for details
In an emergency, the system will automatically apply braking force to avoid or mitigate collisions, accompanied with audible and visible warnings. Please refer to the Manual for details
The system will send audible and visual alarms if it detects a potential risk of collision in front. Please refer to the Manual for details

Note:\nFCW is a safety assistance and cannot cope with all conditions. Whether the function will be triggered depends on actual road conditions. The driver must keep distance from other vehicles, control the driving speed, be ready to brake or steer when necessary and drive in a responsible manner.
Note:\nDOW is ADAS system and cannot completely replace the driver\'s operation. The driver must focus on the road conditions information and drive safely

When the vehicle is stationary and the door is unlocked, and a moving target such as a bicycle or car approaches the vehicle from the rear of the adjacent lanes, the system will make the rearview mirror warning light always on to remind the driver to pay attention to the vehicles coming from behind, and the instrument panel has an icon reminder. When the driver tries to open the door at this time, the rearview mirror warning light flashes with an audible alert. Please refer to the Manual for details
Note:\nThe system is ADAS system and cannot completely replace the driver\'s operation. The driver must focus on the road conditions information and drive safely

When the vehicle is moving and the rear corner MMW radars detect a vehicle approaching quickly from behind in the lane and there is a risk of collision, the vehicle emergency warning light turns on to remind rear vehicle driver. Please refer to the Manual for details
Note:\nRear Cross Traffic Alert (RCTA) is a driving assistance system that should not be relied upon solely, as drivers should remain attentive and cautious at all times to prevent accidents

When reversing, RCTA detects other vehicles driving in the blind area behind the vehicle through the rear corner MMW radars. When the system determines that other vehicles approaching from behind may collide with this vehicle, the exterior rearview mirror warning light flashes with an audible alarm to alert the driver to reduce the possibility of the collision. Please refer to the Manual for details

Note:\nRear Cross Traffic Brake is a safety assistance feature which cannot completely replace the driver\'s operation. The driver needs to always pay attention to the road environment information and drive safely.

When reversing, the Rear Cross Traffic Brake (RCTB) detects other vehicles driving in the blind zone behind the vehicle with the rear corner MMW radar. If the system determines that other vehicles approaching behind are likely to collide with the vehicle, the system automatically performs emergency braking. Please refer to the Manual for details
If this function is turned off, the vehicle cannot slow down automatically on a curve (SOAC), which results in a risk of running out of the lane \nTurn off Speed Adjustment on Curve (SAOC)?
Note:\nThe driver shall concentrate and shall not rely too much on this function, so as to avoid accidents. Please refer to the user manual for details.

Speed Adjustment on Curve (SAOC) is a ADAS function enhancing comfort. When Adaptive Cruise Control/Intelligent Cruise Control (ACC/ICC) is activated, this function can reduce the driving speed automatically on a curve to enhance driving safety and comfort

Note: \nConsidering actual traffic control and possible deviations in map data, the speed limit shown may be different from the actual limit. This function is only for reference. Please follow the actual speed limit information
Speed Limit Forecast (SLF) is an ADAS function. On the road section with speed limit information, this function can display speed limit ahead according to the map data

Intelligent Cruise Control (ICC) is a comfortable ADAS function that helps the driver keep the vehicle at the centre of the current lane and controls the speed based on the set speed and following distance

Note:\nICC is applicable for dry lane with clear markings. In case of adverse weather, slippery roads, blurred markings, exit this function timely. ICC is an ADAS function, and the driver must hold the steering wheel all the time and take over when necessary

To enable Navigate on Driving Assistant (NOA), activate Automatic Emergency Braking (AEB), Interactive Lane Change Assist (ILCA), Driver Monitor Assist (standard), and Auto Valet Parking (AVP). Enable Navigate on Driving Assistant (NOA)?
To enable Highway Navigate on Driving Assistant (HNOA), activate Automatic Emergency Braking (AEB), Interactive Lane Change Assist (ILCA), and Driver Monitor Assist (standard). Enable HNOA?
To enable City Navigate on Driving Assistant (CNOA), activate Automatic Emergency Braking (AEB), Interactive Lane Change Assist (ILCA), and Driver Monitor Assist (standard). Enable CNOA?

Navigate on Driving Assistant (NOA):\nIt is a comfortable ADAS function, applicable to some highways and urban highways (covered by the ADAS Map). Under the effective monitoring of the driver, it can complete the whole process of automatic navigation assisted driving, in which the vehicle automatically drives from the parking space to the getting-on point in the car park - via CNOA - HNOA - CNOA - to the getting-off point in the car park, and then automatically parks into parking space

Note:\nNavigate on Driving Assistant (NOA) is available for some highways covered by the ADAS Map and requires good road conditions such as clear lane lines and non-construction roads. Please refer to the Manual for details. When enabled, the driver is still responsible for the safety of the vehicle all the time. The driver must keep focused and take over the steering wheel when necessary

City Navigate on Driving Assistant (CNOA) is a comfortable ADAS function, which applies to driving on some urban roads (covered by ADAS maps) and allows lane change, obstacle avoidance, speed adjustment and other operations from point A to point B according to the navigation path under the effective monitoring by the driver

Note:\nCity Navigate on Driving Assistant (CNOA) is applicable to some urban roads covered by the ADAS Map and requires good road conditions such as clear lane lines and non-construction roads. Please refer to the Manual for details. When enabled, the driver is still responsible for the safety of the vehicle all the time. The driver must keep focused and take over the steering wheel when necessary
Note:\nThe Traffic Light Attention belongs to ADAS. No matter whether this function is used or not, the driver needs to concentrate on road conditions at all times

Traffic Light Attention (TLA) is a driving assistance feature that, when activated, uses the car\'s cameras to monitor the status of traffic lights ahead in real-time and reminds the driver of changes in the traffic signals
Note:\nTraffic sign recognition belongs to ADAS, which cannot completely replace drivers\' behaviour. Drivers need to pay attention to road traffic sign information at all times

Traffic Sign Recognition includes RSI and SLIF. According to the operating conditions, the system obtains the traffic sign information and the speed limit information that the vehicle should comply with under the current road conditions, which is displayed on the instrument panel or the vehicle system to remind the driver. Please refer to the Manual for details

When the vehicle speed exceeds a certain value, and the vehicle is about to deviate from the lane to reach the edge of the lane or the solid line, or when the oncoming vehicle is approaching and changing lanes which may cause danger, the system is activated and provides reverse steering torque to prevent the vehicle from crossing the edge of the road, and triggers an emergency lane keeping reminder simultaneously. When setting a target SOC, the vehicle would try to keep the real SOC to the target. The default target value is %1$d%%. 
When the destination is convenient for vehicle charging, to make the best use of the electric driving power and reduce the fuel consumption, a LOWER target SOC is recommended.
When the destination is NOT convenient for vehicle charging, and there might be unavoidable traffic jam in the half way, a HIGHER target SOC is recommended.
AUTO/SAVE mode is related to the vehicle energy management priority.
SAVE: Prefer keeping vehicle battery power, and try to get close to the target SOC.
AUTO: Prefer fuel economy, but also take battery power keeping into consideration.

The SOC balance point refers to the target battery holding capacity. The default target value is 15%
When the destination is convenient for vehicle charging, to make the best use of the electric driving power and reduce the fuel consumption, a LOWER SOC balance point is recommended
When the destination is NOT convenient for vehicle charging, and there might be unavoidable traffic jam in the half way, a HIGHER SOC balance point is recommended
AUTO/SAVE mode is related to the vehicle energy management priority
SAVE: Prefer keeping vehicle battery power, and try to get close to the target SOC
AUTO: Prefer fuel economy, but also take battery power save into consideration

The SOC balance point refers to the target battery holding capacity. The default target value is 25%
• If the vehicle can be charged at the destination, it is recommended to lower SOC balance point to make full use of the stored power to drive the vehicle and save fuel consumption;
• If it is not possible to charge at the destination and the route has predictable congestion, mountainous roads and other special conditions, it is recommended to raise the balance point to keep the power and improve the driving experience

AUTO/SAVE is associated with vehicle energy management priority
• AUTO: Give priority to fuel economy and take into account the demand for power maintenance
• SAVE: Give priority to power maintenance, and keep SOC as close as possible to the set value

Wading protection is suitable for waterlogged roads. The vehicle may start the engine forcibly, or maintain exhaust back pressure of the engine to improve the possibility of passing through the wading area and safety of the vehicle. nPlease enable wading protection before driving into the wading area. If the engine is not started successfully after wading protection is enabled, do not drive into the wading area. If the vehicle is driven into the wading area in EV mode, or the engine stalls during wading process, please contact the authorised service centre for overhaul of related parts timely.
After wading protection is enabled, and the engine is started successfully, the following conditions should be met:
● Wading depth < 700 mm 
● Initial SOC > 20% 
● No abnormal condition of the vehicle, and no light alarm in the instrument 
● Avoid driving in turbulent water (flood included) 
● Avoid driving or stopping in the deep water area for a long time 
Compliance with the conditions above will contribute to the safe use of wading protection. However, this function is unable to detect or predict whether the actual water depth increases rapidly, and to predict whether it is safe to continue driving. Please evaluate the driving situation of your vehicle in the wading area by yourself, and enable or disable wading protection in time according to the instructions and the risk alert. 
Considering objective factors such as driving environment, weather, software & hardware, network availability, we cannot guarantee this function works normally at any time. Please actively focus on driving conditions. 
Please prudently allow others to use wading protection for driving safety. Otherwise, BYD will not be liable for damages unless otherwise expressly specified by laws and regulations or BYD is the party in fault.

1. Prior to using the Towing mode, please plan your route appropriately to allow for the reduction in range from towing

4. For safety purposes, once the Towing mode is activated, the vehicle's acceleration performance and maximum speed will be adjusted; other functions including ADAS and park assist will be restricted 
5. When towing, please choose as flat a road as possible; avoid using the Towing mode on wet, icy or steep or wading roads. Do not brake or turn sharply while driving
